title: Housing
summary: Renting, tenant rights, housing defects, moving and finding the correct local or national housing route.
startHere: Identify whether your question is about finding a home, a contract, rent, or a defect.
Use the municipality filter for local services; national tenant guidance remains visible.
Check the responsible official source before sending documents or paying a fee.

title: Work
summary: Employment contracts, wages, working conditions, job-search routes and help with workplace problems.
startHere: Separate job-search questions from contract, pay, dismissal or unsafe-work questions.
Keep your written contract and payslips when asking for help.
Use Work in NL or the responsible inspectorate for current official guidance.

title: Documents
summary: BSN, BRP registration, DigiD, residence documents and other identity or administrative records.

terms: How do I get a BSN

startHere: Choose the document or identifier you need: BSN/BRP, DigiD, residence document or civil record.
For BSN and BRP, use your municipality or an RNI desk according to your situation.
For a lost residence document, follow the IND route and do not rely on generic replacement advice.

title: Healthcare
summary: Finding and registering with a GP, health insurance, pharmacies, urgent care and navigating Dutch healthcare.
startHere: For life-threatening danger call 112; otherwise distinguish routine GP care from urgent out-of-hours care.
Search for a GP near your residence and ask your insurer for help if practices cannot accept you.
Verify insurance duties against your residence and work situation.

title: Education
summary: Primary and secondary schools, newcomer classes, higher education, enrolment and qualification routes.
startHere: Choose primary, secondary, vocational or higher education before selecting a route.
For a child new to Dutch, ask the school or municipality about newcomer or language support.
Check local admission rules and availability directly with the school.

title: Language learning
summary: Dutch courses, NT2 examinations, language support and choosing a learning route.
startHere: Decide whether you need everyday Dutch, work or study Dutch, or a formal examination.
Check whether your integration route sets a required level before paying for a course.
Use DUO for current NT2 examination information.

title: Government
summary: National government services, public administration, official correspondence and finding the responsible authority.
startHere: Identify whether the responsible body is national, provincial or municipal.
Use the sender and reference number on an official letter to find the responsible body.
Share sensitive identifiers only through the authority's verified channel.

title: Banking
summary: Bank accounts, payments, identity checks, fraud awareness and regulated financial-service routes.
startHere: Check whether the provider is authorised before opening an account or investing.
Compare identity requirements and service conditions directly with providers.
Never share login codes or approve an unfamiliar payment.

title: Taxes
summary: Dutch income tax, tax returns, letters, assessments and finding the correct Tax Administration route.
startHere: Identify the tax year and the type of letter or return.
Use Mijn Belastingdienst or an official contact route for personal records.
Do not infer a deadline or amount from a general guide; follow the date on your official notice.

title: Benefits
summary: Healthcare, housing, childcare and child-related benefits, eligibility checks and reporting changes.
startHere: Choose the specific benefit before checking eligibility.
Use your current household, income and residence information in the official calculator or portal.
Report relevant changes through the official Benefits service.

title: SIM & telecom
summary: Mobile subscriptions, prepaid SIM cards, number portability, coverage and telecom consumer rights.
startHere: Choose prepaid or a subscription based on your expected use and documentation.
Compare the total contract terms, not only the introductory price.
Use ACM ConsuWijzer if you have a consumer-rights problem.

officialSources.name: ACM ConsuWijzer — Telephone, internet and television

title: Internet
summary: Home internet, installation, provider switching, contract terms and connection problems.
startHere: Check which networks and providers serve your exact address.
Compare the full contract, installation conditions and cancellation terms.
Keep written confirmation of any switch or cancellation.

officialSources.name: ACM ConsuWijzer — Telephone, internet and television

title: Utilities
summary: Electricity, gas, water, meters, moving notifications and consumer problems with utility contracts.
startHere: Record meter readings and the handover date when moving.
Identify whether the issue concerns the supplier, network operator, landlord or municipality.
Compare contract conditions and use the regulator's consumer guidance for disputes.

title: Transport
summary: Public transport, OV payments, cycling, driving, parking and travel-planning routes.
startHere: Choose public transport, cycling, driving or parking.
Use the operator for a specific journey and national guidance for payment rules.
Check local parking rules on the relevant municipality's official website.

officialSources.name: Government.nl — Mobility, public transport and road safety

title: Rules
summary: National and local rules, permits, duties and identifying which authority sets or enforces a requirement.
startHere: Identify the activity, address and responsible authority.
Separate national law from municipal rules and permits.
Verify the current text or official service before acting.

title: Fines
summary: Traffic and parking fines, official letters, payment routes and finding the correct objection or appeal process.
startHere: Read who issued the fine: municipality, CJIB or another authority.
Use the objection or appeal instructions and date printed on the official notice.
Do not send payment or identity data through an unverified link.

title: Legal help
summary: Finding appropriate legal information, low-threshold advice, representation and urgent protection routes.
startHere: Record the issue, deadline, responsible organisation and documents you have.
Use a low-threshold legal information service to identify the correct route.
Treat court or objection deadlines as urgent and follow the official notice.

title: Family
summary: Marriage, partnership, family records, family migration and finding the relevant official route.
startHere: Separate municipal civil-status matters from IND family-migration matters.
Check whether foreign documents need translation or legalisation on the responsible authority's site.
Use the exact route for your relationship and residence situation.

title: Children
summary: Birth registration, childcare, school, youth healthcare and services for parents and children.
startHere: Choose birth registration, childcare, school, health or family support.
Use your municipality for local registration and support routes.
Verify benefit and childcare requirements separately with the responsible service.

title: Safety
summary: Police contact, reporting crime, scams, domestic safety and non-emergency support.
startHere: If there is immediate danger, use the emergency route.
For non-emergency police matters, use the verified national police channel.
Preserve messages, payment records or other evidence without sharing it publicly.

title: Emergency
summary: Immediate danger, urgent medical help and verified emergency contact routes in the Netherlands.
startHere: For immediate danger to life or property, call 112.
For urgent but non-life-threatening medical needs, contact your GP or the out-of-hours GP service.
Do not delay emergency contact while searching for general information.

title: Shopping
summary: Consumer rights, returns, warranties, online purchases, complaints and avoiding misleading sellers.
startHere: Keep the order, receipt, seller terms and written communication.
Identify whether the purchase was online, in a shop or from a private seller.
Use ACM ConsuWijzer for current Dutch consumer guidance.

title: Daily life
summary: Everyday practical questions, local routines, neighbourhood services and directing a question to the right domain.
startHere: Name the task you need to complete rather than searching only for a broad topic.
Add your municipality when the answer depends on local services.
Use a specialised domain for legal, health, financial or emergency questions.

title: Pets
summary: Bringing, registering and caring for pets, travel requirements and local animal-related rules.
startHere: For travel, check the animal, origin country and travel date against current official requirements.
For local registration or tax, use the municipality's official site.
Use a veterinarian for individual animal-health advice.

officialSources.name: Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority

title: Business
summary: Starting and running a business, registration, tax, permits, hiring and official entrepreneur support.
startHere: Check whether your residence status allows the intended work or business activity.
Use the official entrepreneur checklist to identify registration, tax and permit duties.
Keep private commercial offers separate from mandatory public registrations.

title: Integration
summary: Civic integration, official notices, learning routes, examinations and support from the municipality or DUO.
startHere: Check which law and integration route apply to the date and basis of your obligation.
Use the municipality and DUO roles shown in your official notice.
Verify examination and payment information before booking or paying.

title: Municipal services
summary: Registration, address changes, civil records, permits, waste, parking and other services provided by your municipality.
startHere: Select your municipality because services and forms are local.
Choose the exact task, such as BRP registration, moving, a certificate, parking or waste.
Open the municipality's official site from its YouNew municipality page.
